lane: WHAT MADE SUBEXPONENTIAL DLP WORK ELSEWHERE (finite-field DLP, Drinfeld modules, class groups / high-genus Jacobians, E over extension fields, isogeny structural results) and whether ECDLP over F_p or F_{2^prime} has an untried analogue

mechanisms.mechanism: Finite-field DLP, small/fixed characteristic (Joux 2013 L(1/4); BGJT 2014 heuristic QP; GKZ 2018 rigorous QP for infinite families via zig-zag descent; Kleinjung-Wesolowski 2019/2021 rigorous QP for all fixed-characteristic fields; GKLWZ 2020/21 2^30750 record; Joux-Pierrot elliptic bases)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: (a) a sub-additive SIZE: degree of a polynomial/function/divisor, deg(fg)=deg f+deg g, so 'smooth' = splits into low-degree factors and smoothness probability is a Dickman-type function of the degree ratio; (b) a QUOTIENT/FILTRATION: F_{q^n} = F_q[x]/(I) or F_q(E)/I filtered by degree, with Frobenius acting as a LOW-DEGREE rational map (x^q = h0/h1, or translation by a point Q of order n in the K-W elliptic model), so Frobenius does not blow up degree; (c) a dense supply of relations among degree-1 elements: the PGL_2-orbit of x^q - x consists of polynomials that split completely over F_q (K-W Section 3), i.e. a positive-density set of 'systematic' relations; (d) a DESCENT (zig-zag 4->3->2 eliminations, trap divisors avoided) that reduces an arbitrary element to the factor base with only polylog depth.
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: E(F_p): no degree function on points (Heights closure: sums of small points are not small), Frobenius is trivial, no low-degree membership for any subset (No-subfield closure, RESEARCH_PRIME_FIELD_BREAKTHROUGH_PROGRAM 2.3). The only 'size' available is x as an integer mod p (Lattice-reach closure: J-M reach 1/80 vs needed 1/5 at m=4). E(F_{2^131}): Frobenius exists but the only subfield is F_2 and ord_131(2)=130, so no Frobenius-stable subspace (closure); Frobenius-stable NON-subspace bases (trace-spectrum, Hamming ball, mu_263, Couveignes-Lercier algebraic-group points/elliptic periods) are lever 6, unmeasured. No analogue of (c): there is no positive-density family of 'automatically splitting' relations because the summation-cover monodromy closure says fibres split completely only on the factor-base locus and mean yield is a double count. Verdict: closed except lever 6 and the descent idea has no analogue (no size to descend in).

mechanisms.mechanism: Finite-field DLP, medium/large characteristic (NFS, TNFS/exTNFS, Factory, Galois automorphisms in LA)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: Two number-field 'sides' with a common quotient map to F_{p^n}; smoothness of ideal norms (sub-multiplicative size); order-k Galois automorphisms give factor k in sieving and k^2 in linear algebra (Al Aswad-Pierrot-Thome 2026 for k=6,12); Factory: one precomputation shared by a constant fraction of all fields of given approximate size and degree (Chebotarev).
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: Symmetry gains are already in the programme's symmetry inventory (Frobenius /n relations, /n^2 LA; Faugere-Svartz blocks 31-128x; lever 5 Frobenius-equivariant F4), and are polynomial in n by the Symmetry inventory closure. Shared precomputation across an isogeny class / multi-target is closed (LEAD-STR-isogeny-transport-preprocessing, LEAD-ICB-multi-target-and-portfolio closed_obstructed; Bernstein-Lange equal-advice audits). No new door.

mechanisms.mechanism: Drinfeld-module DLP and Drinfeld isogeny problems (Scanlon 2001; Joux-Narayanan 2019; Wesolowski 2022; Leudiere-Spaenlehauer 2022-24)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: NOT index calculus. The underlying group is G_a(k) (the additive group of the finite field) and the A=F_q[T]-action phi_a is an F_q-LINEAR map of k; on a fixed finite field the whole Drinfeld module is a commutative algebra of F_p-linear maps, so 'find a with phi_a(x)=y' is linear algebra in the cyclic A-module generated by x (Scanlon Prop. 4, O(m^{1+omega})). Isogenies u between Drinfeld modules are elements of k{tau} with u phi_T = psi_T u, LINEAR in the coefficients of u, so bounded-tau-degree isogenies and a basis of Hom are found by linear algebra (Wesolowski 2022/438 Thm 1.1); hence the CRS-type group action of a function-field class group (Jacobian of imaginary hyperelliptic curve) on Drinfeld modules is invertible in polynomial time.
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: The brief (section 3 item 14) says the Drinfeld DLP 'is broken by index calculus' - the literature says it is broken by LINEARITY. The structural difference is exactly that E's group law is not F_q-linear in any coordinate; the only place E(F_q) becomes an additive group linear over the base field is the formal group E_1(Q_p)/E_2(Q_p) = F_p^+ after a p-adic lift, which is the Smart/Satoh-Araki/Semaev anomalous attack and works only when the trace-one condition puts the DLP into that quotient (LEAD-TRF-anomalous-padic-lift closed_known; LEAD-TRF-padic-canonical-section closed_obstructed; LEAD-EXO-padic-jet-canonical-lift closed_obstructed). Also, Hom(E,E') is a Z-module of rank <= 4 with no F_q-vector-space structure, so the Wesolowski linear-algebra isogeny algorithm has no EC analogue. Verdict: Drinfeld analogy is a wall, not a door; it sharpens the programme's p-adic closures and answers item 14.

mechanisms.mechanism: Class groups of number fields and Jacobians of high-genus / low-degree curves (Hafner-McCurley; Enge-Gaudry 2002 L(1/2) framework; Enge-Gaudry-Thome 2011 L(1/3); Diem 2006 plane curves of small degree Õ(q^{2-2/(d-2)}), Õ(q) for plane quartics; de Boer-Pellet-Mary-Wesolowski 2025/26 rigorous ERH subexp class groups)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: A monoid with a NORM (sub-multiplicative size) and unique factorisation into primes (ideals / places), so that a random element of a class can be rerandomised until its representative is B-smooth, with probability given by a Dickman-type count; for curves, reduced divisors of degree <= g are represented by polynomials of degree <= g in Mumford form (genus = room for smoothness); for low-degree plane models, the linear system of lines (Diem) or small-degree functions (EGT) gives relations among d points with d << g; rigour comes from being able to sample a random ideal of a class inside a dense family S.S_B (dBPW 2025).
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: g=1: a reduced divisor is one point, nothing to factor; the plane model is a cubic (d=3=g+2) so Diem's line-relation IS the group law. Same-field embeddings of E as an isogeny factor of a genus-g Jacobian: LEAD-TRF-same-field-genus-g-embedding closed_obstructed; LEAD-EXO-split-jacobian-projection closed_obstructed. Weil restriction to higher genus needs an extension field (GHS: LEAD-TRF-ghs-binary-composite closed_known; Song Tian 2020 for prime-order E/F_{q^3} via (l,l,l)-isogeny of the Weil restriction: covered by LEAD-TRF-weil-restriction-jacobian-class open_next_step but needs n>=3). Prime n=131 and F_p have no intermediate field. Verdict: closed; the one untested idea from this family is the dBPW 'sample inside a dense family' lemma as a RIGOUR tool, not a speed tool.
closure_refs: Hyperelliptic index calculus and the genus threshold (known_bound)

mechanisms.mechanism: Elliptic curves over extension fields F_{q^n} (Gaudry 2004/2009 Õ(q^{2-2/n}); Diem 2011/2013 rigorous subexp for n->inf, n/log q->0; Joux-Vitse 2010-12 (n-1)-decomposition and cover+decomposition on F_{p^6}; Petit-Quisquater 2012 first-fall-degree heuristic for F_{2^n}; GGMP 2020 Frobenius-invariant bases on subfield curves)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: A SUBFIELD F_q c F_{q^n}: the factor base {P : x(P) in F_q} is a 1-dimensional subvariety of the n-dimensional Weil restriction, membership is LINEAR after Weil descent (x^q = x becomes n-1 linear equations), and decomposition of a point into n factor-base points is a zero-dimensional system S_{n+1}(x_1..x_n, x(R)) of n equations in n F_q-unknowns; cost is governed by the solving degree, which for fixed n is bounded (Gaudry) and for growing n is the first/last-fall-degree question (Petit-Quisquater vs HKYY).
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: F_p: no subfield -> the programme's digit (base-B) presentation lever 9 is the only analogue (LEAD-ICP-digit-presentation-solving-degree open_next_step) and LEAD-ICP-extension-field-embedding is closed_obstructed. F_{2^131}: the only subfield is F_2, Weil descent to F_2 gives Boolean systems whose last fall degree growth is lever 1 (KN-OPEN-8f3d27 etc.); first fall degree is a constant of the presentation (closure). Subfield-curve Frobenius-invariant bases (GGMP 2020) are in the frontier as known_mechanism. Verdict: fully in atlas; the extension-field mechanism is the ancestor of everything the programme measures.
closure_refs: First fall degree is a constant of the presentation
'Diem: rigorous subexponential ECDLP for suitable n' (known_bound)

mechanisms.mechanism: Isogeny world 2021-2026 (Wesolowski 2021 path <-> EndRing; Castryck-Decru / Maino-Martindale-Panny-Pope-Wesolowski / Robert 2022 Kani attacks; Robert 2022 embedding lemma: End of ordinary E in poly time given factorisation of Delta_pi, canonical lifts; Page-Robert Clapoti 2023, PEGASIS 2025 poly-time class-group action; Castryck et al. 2023 self-pairing weak instances; Herledan Le Merdy-Wesolowski 2025 unconditional equivalences; Delgado 2026-09 and Ouyang-Wei-Xu 2026-10 unconditional p^{1/3} OneEnd; Galbraith 2024/25 tall volcanoes q^{1/4})
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: TORSION-POINT INFORMATION: images of a basis of E[N] under the secret isogeny phi, with N^2 > deg phi, determine phi via Kani's lemma as a component of an (N,N)-isogeny of E^2 (or E^4, E^8); END-RING AS COMPLETE INVARIANT: supersingular End(E) is a maximal order in a quaternion algebra with efficiently checkable structure (KLPT), and OneEnd -> EndRing -> path are poly-time equivalent; CLASS-GROUP ACTION: the ideal class group of the orientation order acts freely and transitively, ideals have norms and factor into primes (index calculus / Hafner-McCurley in the class group), and the action is now poly-time evaluable (Clapoti/PEGASIS); SMOOTHNESS OF ISOGENY DEGREES (Delgado; Ouyang-Wei-Xu) gives unconditional meet-in-the-middle.
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: Q=[k]P is the image of ONE point under the endomorphism [k]; Kani needs images of a full E[N]-basis with N^2 > k^2 ~ r^2, and E(F_q)[N] for the only rational N (N | #E) is the prime-order group itself, so 'torsion information' for [k] IS the DLP; LEAD-TRF-second-torsion-direction (Kani/Robert graph kernels, Richelot gluing) is closed_obstructed. End-ring and class-group structure live on the ISOGENY GRAPH, not inside E(F_q): group order is an isogeny invariant (Tate) and homomorphic transport changes the decomposition count by exactly |kappa|^{m-1} (Transport conservation), so Clapoti/PEGASIS/Galbraith q^{1/4} only make the already-closed random self-reduction cheaper (LEAD-STR-jmv-random-self-reduction closed_known; LEAD-STR-isogeny-class-generic-invariance closed_obstructed). Self-pairings need a known secret degree and oriented curves (LEAD-ICP-self-pairing-prime-order, LEAD-TRF-one-point-self-pairing closed_obstructed). Robert's canonical-lift algorithm is a tool for LEAD-TRF-cm-canonical-lift-heights (closed_obstructed by heights). The only live bridge is LEAD-STR-class-group-ecdlp-bridge open_next_step, and the self-pairing paper shows the direction Cl(O)-vectorisation -> something only when a degree is known. Verdict: closed; recent results strengthen, not weaken, the walls.

mechanisms.mechanism: Lower-bound side, 2024-2026 (Corrigan-Gibbs-Henzinger-Wu structured GGM, EUROCRYPT 2026; Hhan 2024 compression-lemma bounds incl. an index-calculus model; Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026-10 polynomial approximation of dlog)
mechanisms.structural_ingredient: Structured GGM: an algorithm that exploits non-generic structure of at most a delta fraction of group elements needs Omega(min(sqrt q, 1/delta)) time; tight subexponential lower bound for 'smooth-integer index calculus but otherwise generic', and analogous bounds for small integers, smooth polynomials and elliptic-curve points. KKS: any degree-D polynomial over F_p agrees with log on <= ~sqrt(Dp) inputs (Johnson bound via list decoding), O(p^{2/5}) for affine (sum-product).
mechanisms.ecdlp_analogue_status: Directly relevant to rule 5 (non-genericity certificate B.D^2 << N): the structured-GGM bound says a factor base that is a delta = B/r fraction of the group, used generically otherwise, costs >= min(sqrt r, r/B) - i.e. the 'representation-dependent step' must itself be the non-generic part, which is the programme's 'only door is the field representation'. KKS gives a template for a rigorous wall on polynomial x-functional filters (lever 8, KN-OPEN-91d4f6) if ported to E(F_p) (classical EC analogues: Lange-Winterhof interpolation bounds, not re-verified here). Novel to the programme as formal tools.

papers.title: Discrete logarithms in quasi-polynomial time in finite fields of fixed characteristic
papers.authors: Thorsten Kleinjung, Benjamin Wesolowski
papers.date: 2019-06 (arXiv 1906.10668 / ePrint 2019/751); J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2021 (announced ANTS XIII 2018)
papers.summary: Proves DLP in F_{p^n}^* in expected time (pn)^{2 log_2 n + O(1)}. Avoids the unproven h1 x^q - h0 field model: uses an ELLIPTIC-CURVE MODEL (Def. 2.1): ordinary E/F_q, rational point Q of order n, irreducible divisor I of degree n with f o phi_q = f o tau_Q mod I, so F_q[I] = F_{q^n} and Frobenius acts as translation by Q; existence for F_{p^{rn}}, r=O(log n), from Watkins' theorem. Descent is zig-zag (4->3, 3->2 eliminations, trap divisors avoided); relations come from the PGL_2-orbit of x^q - x, every member of which splits completely over F_q.
papers.relevance: The canonical 'what made it work': sub-additive degree + Frobenius as a low-degree (translation) map + a positive-density family of automatically-splitting polynomials. ECDLP over F_p has none of the three (Heights, No-subfield, Summation-cover monodromy closures). Over F_{2^131} the Frobenius exists but ord_131(2)=130 kills Frobenius-stable subspaces; the elliptic-model idea run backwards (use E-translation structure to pick a base in F_{2^131}) is exactly the Couveignes-Lercier/elliptic-periods item of lever 6, never measured.
papers.suggested_route: No new route from the FF side; the only live cell is lever 6 (Couveignes-Lercier algebraic-group points / cyclotomic-sparse base A2). Toy falsifier: build F_{2^n} (n prime, 13..31) as F_2(E)/I with Frobenius = translation by Q of order n, take as factor base the degree-<=1 'functions' and measure (i) Frobenius-orbit closure, (ii) fall degree of the descended S_3/S_4 vs the standard polynomial-basis subspace at equal dimension; the Frontier closure predicts no change in d_ff and a ratio within the symmetry constant.

papers.title: On the discrete logarithm problem in finite fields of fixed characteristic (zig-zag descent) and On the powers of 2 (Göloğlu-Joux 2019 simplified degree-2 elimination)
papers.authors: Robert Granger, Thorsten Kleinjung, Jens Zumbrägel; Faruk Göloğlu, Antoine Joux (2019)
papers.date: arXiv 1507.01495 (2015-07); Trans. AMS 370 (2018) 3129-3145; ePrint 2014/300; Math. Comp. 88 (2019) 'A simplified approach to rigorous degree 2 elimination'
papers.summary: First rigorous quasi-polynomial DLP for infinitely many explicit extension fields of each characteristic, via repeated degree-two elimination ('zig-zag' descent built only from the on-the-fly degree-2 elimination of Göloğlu-Granger-McGuire-Zumbrägel), conditional on a conjecture about irreducible polynomials of a certain form later removed by Kleinjung-Wesolowski's model. Göloğlu-Joux 2019 gives a simplified proof of the degree-2 elimination.
papers.relevance: Structural ingredient: elimination of an irreducible of degree 2d into degree-d ones by solving a small linear system whose coefficients live in the Frobenius-twisted polynomial identity; depth log n. Needs a degree filtration and a Frobenius acting with bounded degree. No ECDLP analogue: there is no filtration on E(F_p) in which [k] or point addition has bounded 'degree' (Heights closure; the division polynomial of [k] has degree k^2).
papers.suggested_route: None (wall). Record the obstruction precisely: a descent needs a size s with s(P+Q) <= s(P)+s(Q)+O(1) and a cheap map lowering s; on E(F_p) the only candidate (canonical height after lifting) satisfies the parallelogram law, which is the Heights closure.

papers.title: Computation of a 30750-bit binary field discrete logarithm
papers.authors: Robert Granger, Thorsten Kleinjung, Arjen Lenstra, Benjamin Wesolowski, Jens Zumbrägel
papers.summary: Record DLP in F_{2^30750}, ~2900 core-years, first large-scale recursive use of the GKZ elimination step; eliminates small-degree irreducibles without Gröbner bases (the pre-2013 records all needed them).
papers.relevance: Data point for the brief's 'what made subexponential DLP work': the practical gain came from replacing Gröbner solves by linear-algebra eliminations that exist only because of the degree filtration. The programme's binary IC is stuck precisely on Gröbner solving degree (lever 1, 4, 5); there is no analogous linear elimination because Weil-descended S_{m+1} has no degree-lowering map (first fall degree constant of the presentation).
papers.suggested_route: Accounting only: compare GAE cost per relation of the 2^30750 computation (publicly ~2900 core-years for a field of 30750 bits) against the programme's binary n=45 cells to calibrate what 'a working descent' buys; no experiment proposed.

papers.title: Algorithmic aspects of elliptic bases in finite field discrete logarithm algorithms
papers.authors: Antoine Joux, Cécile Pierrot
papers.date: ePrint 2019/782 (2019-07, rev. 2022-10); Advances in Mathematics of Communications 2022
papers.summary: Uses Couveignes-Lercier elliptic bases (F_{q^n} represented through an elliptic curve with Frobenius = translation by a point of order n) as the field representation for heuristic Frobenius-representation DLP algorithms; a different curve model lets the earlier techniques carry over; experiments in F_{3^1345} comparable to leading practical methods.
papers.relevance: Shows elliptic-curve structure is useful FOR finite-field DLP (the curve supplies the automorphism and a 'nice' basis), not the other way round. For the programme it is the literature anchor of lever 6 item 'Couveignes-Lercier algebraic-group points' and of the cyclotomic-sparse base A2: a base in F_{2^131} defined by translation-by-Q structure on an auxiliary curve with a point of order 131 (exists iff 131 | #E'(F_2^k) for the auxiliary curve over the right field).
papers.suggested_route: Toy: for n in {13,17,19,23,29,31}, find an auxiliary ordinary E'/F_2 (or F_4) with a point Q of order n and realise F_{2^n} = F_2(E')/I; define factor base = points of the target curve whose x-coordinate is a degree-<=1 element in this elliptic basis; measure relation yield and the Boolean fall degree of the descended S_3 vs a random subspace of equal dimension. Prediction under closures: identical d_ff, yield within symmetry constant. Any yield excess beyond 2x would be the first representation-dependent base effect at prime n.

papers.title: High-Order Galois Automorphisms for TNFS Linear Algebra
papers.authors: Haetham Al Aswad, Cécile Pierrot, Emmanuel Thomé
papers.summary: TNFS for F_{p^6}, F_{p^12}: order-k Galois automorphisms already give factor k in relation collection; the paper constructs their use in the linear-algebra step for k=6 and k=12 (previously only k=2), estimated speedups ~36 and ~144 (= k^2), SageMath implementation on small examples. No record computation in this paper (the 2021 De Micheli-Gaudry-Pierrot 521-bit F_{p^6} TNFS record is the cited baseline; not opened here).
papers.relevance: Confirms the k^2 linear-algebra gain for a cyclic symmetry group, the same accounting the programme already uses for Frobenius (/n relations, /n^2 LA) and for lever 5 Frobenius-equivariant F4 on the barrel system. Polynomial in n, cannot change an exponent (Symmetry inventory closure).
papers.suggested_route: Engineering only: port the 2026/560 block-circulant trick (eigenvector/character decomposition of the automorphism) to the programme's orbit-folded relation matrix as a check on the claimed /n^2; if the programme's orbit LA already achieves /n^2 this is 'accounting', else 'engineering'.

papers.title: Discrete Logarithm Factory
papers.authors: Haetham Al Aswad, Cécile Pierrot, Emmanuel Thomé
papers.summary: Extends the NFS 'Factory' idea to F_{p^n} of medium/large characteristic: one precomputation depending only on the approximate size and the extension degree serves a constant fraction of all fields with those parameters (density via Chebotarev); combined with TNFS/SNFS it improves asymptotic complexity; MNFS gains are subsumed.
papers.relevance: Structural ingredient: a shared algebraic object (number field) with maps to many target fields. ECDLP analogue would be a shared object mapping to many curves: the isogeny class. Closed: group order is an isogeny invariant and shared tables across a class are generic advice (LEAD-STR-isogeny-transport-preprocessing closed_obstructed; equal-advice Bernstein-Lange audits).
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Public key cryptosystems based on Drinfeld modules are insecure
papers.authors: Thomas Scanlon
papers.summary: Read in full. Defines the Drinfeld-module DLP (given phi: A -> k{F}, x, y in k, find a in A with phi(a)(x)=y) and inversion problem and gives polynomial-time algorithms (Props. 2-4, O(m^{1+omega}) field ops, m = dim_{F_p} k). Mechanism, quoted: 'while a Drinfeld module is generically nonlinear, when considered on a fixed finite field it may be regarded as a linear object' - phi(A) is a commutative subalgebra of M_m(F_p); the cyclic A-module generated by x has an F_p-basis {phi(s^i t^j)(x)} and y is expressed in that basis by linear algebra. NOT index calculus.
papers.relevance: Answers brief section 3 item 14 ('the DLP on Drinfeld modules is broken by index calculus; what makes E(F_q) resist?'): it is broken by F_q-LINEARITY of the scalar action on the additive group G_a(k). The EC counterpart is the formal-group linearisation E_1(Q_p)/E_2 = F_p^+ used by the anomalous attack, available only when the trace-one condition moves the DLP into that quotient (LEAD-TRF-anomalous-padic-lift closed_known); all other p-adic/canonical-lift linearisations are closed (LEAD-TRF-padic-canonical-section, LEAD-EXO-padic-jet-canonical-lift closed_obstructed). The brief's item 14 wording should be corrected.
papers.suggested_route: Falsifier for the 'structural difference' question (toy, exact): for E/F_p (p ~ 2^20) check that no F_p-linear (or F_p-affine) map L on any coordinate chart satisfies L(x(kP)) = k-dependent linear function of L(x(P)) for all P - i.e. compute the F_p-dimension of the span of {x([k]P) : P} relations; contrast with the Drinfeld case where dim of the A-module is <= m. Expected result: the Mordell-Weil group has no F_p-linear structure except in the formal group; this is a one-page theorem (Scanlon's argument needs End to act through Hom(k,+)), so classify as 'accounting/closure' not experiment.

papers.title: Drinfeld modules may not be for isogeny based cryptography
papers.authors: Antoine Joux, Anand Kumar Narayanan
papers.summary: Abstract read; PDF blocked (403). States 'the Drinfeld module discrete logarithm problem is easy even on a classical computer' (citing the Scanlon-type linearity), formulates Drinfeld analogues of SIDH and CSIDH and breaks them with classical polynomial-time algorithms. Mechanism (UNVERIFIED from this paper; consistent with Wesolowski 2022/438): isogenies u in k{tau} between rank-2 Drinfeld modules satisfy u phi_T = psi_T u, linear in the coefficients of u, so bounded-degree isogenies are found by F_q-linear algebra; the Frobenius endomorphism and its characteristic polynomial give the isogeny class directly.
papers.relevance: Same wall as Scanlon from the isogeny side: Hom between Drinfeld modules is an F_q-vector space of twisted polynomials, Hom(E,E') is a rank <= 4 Z-module with no base-field-linear structure. Identifies precisely why the isogeny-world structural results (Kani, End-ring) do not linearise ECDLP.
papers.suggested_route: Literature only; obtain the PDF via a browser and confirm the mechanism before citing it in the report. No experiment.

papers.title: Computing isogenies between finite Drinfeld modules
papers.authors: Benjamin Wesolowski
papers.summary: Theorem 1.1 (via search): given n and two Drinfeld modules over a finite field, finds an isogeny of tau-degree n or proves none exists in time polynomial in n and the input, and returns a basis of the F_q-linear space of morphisms of degree <= n. Breaks Drinfeld analogues of isogeny-based cryptosystems (any rank), superseding Joux-Narayanan's rank-2 attack.
papers.relevance: Structural ingredient: the morphism space is a finite-dimensional F_q-vector space with a linear defining equation. For elliptic curves the analogous 'find an isogeny of given degree' is the hard isogeny problem (and the 2022 Kani attacks need torsion images). For ECDLP: nothing; records why 'isogeny structure' cannot be used to linearise [k].
papers.suggested_route: None (wall). Cite together with Scanlon as the two-line answer to brief item 14.

papers.title: Computing a group action from the class field theory of imaginary hyperelliptic function fields
papers.authors: Antoine Leudière, Pierre-Jean Spaenlehauer
papers.date: 2022-03-14 (arXiv 2203.06970 v1) ... v6 2024-03-12; Journal of Symbolic Computation
papers.summary: A simply transitive commutative group action of the Jacobian of an imaginary hyperelliptic curve over F_q on isomorphism classes of Drinfeld F_q[X]-modules (function-field analogue of CRS); efficient C++/NTL evaluation; inversion reduces to finding isogenies of fixed tau-degree, solvable in polynomial time by Wesolowski's algorithm, so the cryptographic application was removed in revision.
papers.relevance: The full function-field mirror of 'class group acts on curves' exists and is broken by linearity, not by index calculus on the class group. Reinforces that LEAD-STR-class-group-ecdlp-bridge, if it ever closes a loop, cannot go through a Drinfeld-style linearisation.
papers.suggested_route: None; literature anchor.

papers.title: Rigorous methods for computational number theory
papers.authors: Koen de Boer, Alice Pellet-Mary, Benjamin Wesolowski
papers.summary: First provably probabilistic-subexponential algorithm for class and unit groups of arbitrary number fields under ERH. Key tool: given a class [a], sample an ideal b in that class lying in S.S_B for any chosen family S (e.g. primes -> near-prime ideals, dense and efficiently factorable) with probability proportional to the density of S; the case S = S_B (smooth ideals) is the step index calculus had only heuristically.
papers.relevance: Structural ingredient: rerandomisation within a class that lands in a dense, recognisable, factorable family. ECDLP has free rerandomisation (P -> P + rG) but no family that is both dense and 'factorable' (the programme's 'invertible hint subset' lever 8: dense, recognisable AND invertible subsets of E(F_p)). The dBPW lemma is exactly the rigour template such a subset would need.
papers.suggested_route: Theory note, not experiment: write the ECDLP analogue of the sampling lemma - 'for a subset S of E(F_p) of density delta, the walk P + rG hits S in 1/delta steps' - and show that unless membership in S is decided non-generically (field representation), the resulting algorithm is generic with advice |S| and hits the Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan line. Then state what property of S (beyond density) replaces 'factorable': a map S -> (small group)^m that is additive on sums. This is a reformulation of KN-OPEN-91d4f6, giving it a precise target.

papers.title: A general framework for subexponential discrete logarithm algorithms; Computing discrete logarithms in high-genus hyperelliptic Jacobians in provably subexponential time
papers.authors: Andreas Enge, Pierrick Gaudry (2002); Andreas Enge (2002)
papers.summary: Framework for L(1/2) index calculus in any finite abelian group 'which possesses an analogue to the unique prime decomposition' (abstract); applied to F_q^* recovers the fastest rigorous bounds, to high-genus hyperelliptic Jacobians gives provable subexponential time when g/log q is large enough.
papers.relevance: States the structural axiom in one phrase: a norm plus unique factorisation. E(F_q) with g=1 has a one-element 'Mumford representation' (a point) and no factorisation; the programme's heights closure says lifting to Q to get a norm fails. Frontier row 'Hyperelliptic index calculus and the genus threshold' already encodes this.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: An L(1/3) discrete logarithm algorithm for low degree curves
papers.authors: Andreas Enge, Pierrick Gaudry, Emmanuel Thomé
papers.summary: For plane curves whose degrees in X and Y are small relative to the genus, computes group structure and DLs in L_{q^g}(1/3, O(1)) with NFS/FFS-type heuristics: relations from functions of low degree whose divisors are smooth with respect to a factor base of small-degree places, with a two-sided (sieve-like) construction.
papers.relevance: Ingredient: a filtration (degree in x,y) where the ambient genus is much larger than the degree of the relation-producing functions. For E, genus = 1 = degree scale; no slack. Closed under the same-field genus-g embedding closure.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Index calculus in class groups of plane curves of small degree (plane quartics Õ(q)); with Diem-Thomé (genus 3 non-hyperelliptic) and Smith's isogeny from hyperelliptic genus 3
papers.authors: Claus Diem (2005/2006); Claus Diem, Emmanuel Thomé (2008); Benjamin Smith (2007/2009)
papers.date: ePrint 2005/119 (2005-04); ANTS VII 2006; Math. Comp. 2007; Smith ePrint 2007/428, J. Cryptology 2009
papers.summary: For a curve with a plane model of degree d >= 4, DLP in the degree-0 class group in Õ(q^{2-2/(d-2)}); for d=4 (genus 3 non-hyperelliptic) Õ(q), i.e. exponent 1/3 of the group size q^3. Relations: lines through two factor-base points meet the curve in d-2 further points. Smith transfers a large fraction of hyperelliptic genus-3 Jacobians to non-hyperelliptic ones by explicit (2,2,2)-isogenies.
papers.relevance: Ingredient: a low-degree plane model with g ~ d^2/2 >> d so that a 'line relation' involves d points of a group of size q^g. For E (d=3,g=1) the line relation is the group law itself. The programme's same-field route (E as isogeny factor of a genus-3 Jacobian over F_p, then Diem) is LEAD-TRF-same-field-genus-g-embedding closed_obstructed and LEAD-TRF-odd-char-descent-smith-quartic open_blocked (needs odd-characteristic extension field).
papers.suggested_route: None beyond the filed Prym/same-field follow-ups (lever 10), which the closure already prices.

papers.title: Index calculus for abelian varieties and the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem
papers.authors: Pierrick Gaudry
papers.summary: For E over F_{q^n} with n fixed, factor base = points with x in F_q (a curve inside the n-dimensional Weil restriction), decomposition of R into n base points via Semaev's S_{n+1} and Weil descent; heuristic Õ(q^{2-2/n}) beating rho (q^{n/2}) for n >= 3 with a double-large-prime variant.
papers.relevance: Origin of everything the programme runs. Ingredient: subfield -> linear membership after descent -> zero-dimensional system of n equations in n unknowns. Programme closures: No subfield (F_p), prime n (F_{2^131}), LEAD-ICP-extension-field-embedding closed_obstructed.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves (I, Compositio 2011) and II (Algebra & Number Theory 2013)
papers.authors: Claus Diem
papers.summary: I (abstract verified): for sequences (q_i), (n_i) with n_i -> infinity and n_i/log q_i -> 0, ECDLP over F_{q_i^{n_i}} in subexponential expected time (q_i^{n_i})^{o(1)}; and a specific sequence of finite fields with expected time e^{O((log q_i)^{2/3})}. II (abstract NOT fetched; from memory, unverified): rigorous Õ(q^{2-2/n}) for fixed n >= 2 and related polynomial-factor results, using the factor base x in F_q and a rigorous analysis of the decomposition system.
papers.relevance: The only RIGOROUS subexponential ECDLP results; both require n -> infinity with a subfield. Frontier row 'Diem: rigorous subexponential ECDLP for suitable n'.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem over small degree extension fields (static DH on E(F_{q^5})) and Cover and decomposition index calculus on elliptic curves made practical (F_{p^6})
papers.authors: Antoine Joux, Vanessa Vitse
papers.summary: (n-1)-point decompositions (one fewer summand, far cheaper Gröbner solve at the price of a q-fold smaller yield) make n=5 practical for oracle-assisted static DH; cover (GHS-type, genus-3 hyperelliptic cover of a weak class of E/F_{p^6} over F_{p^2}) + Nagao decomposition over F_{p^2} breaks 'seemingly secure' 130-bit E(F_{p^6}) instances.
papers.relevance: Frontier rows 'Joux-Vitse n-1 decomposition and oracle-assisted static DH', 'ecGFp5 ... published estimates'; atlas LEAD-ICP-gfp5-oa-sdhp-jv open_next_step, LEAD-TRF-jv-sieve-fp6-weak-class open_next_step, LEAD-TRF-jv-nagao-genus2-cover-decomp closed_dominated. Needs intermediate field or weak class.
papers.suggested_route: Already filed (gfp5 and fp6 weak-class leads).

papers.title: On polynomial systems arising from a Weil descent
papers.authors: Christophe Petit, Jean-Jacques Quisquater
papers.summary: Under a first-fall-degree assumption, Weil-descended Semaev systems over F_{2^n} are solved by Gröbner bases in time giving heuristic ECDLP cost O(2^{c n^{2/3} log n}), c < 2; later disputed (HKYY 2015 computational evidence against; Huang-Petit-Shinohara-Takagi 2015 partial support; Kousidis-Wiemers 2019 improved fall degree m^2-m+1).
papers.relevance: The one subexponential CLAIM for prime-degree binary ECDLP, and the programme's central open lever 1 (growth of last fall degree). Frontier 'dispute' rows cover it exactly.
papers.suggested_route: Lever 1 as stated in the brief (grid over (n, l, m >= 3) with closure certificates).

papers.title: On the last fall degree of Weil descent polynomial systems
papers.authors: Ming-Deh Huang
papers.summary: For a (not necessarily zero-dimensional) system F over k with Weil descent F' over a subfield k', proves a theorem relating the last fall degree of the auxiliary system F'_1 (zero set = k'-points of F') to that of F_1 (zero set = k-points of F); application: upper bounds on the last fall degree of descended systems of linearized polynomials.
papers.relevance: Extends HKYY 2015 (zero-dimensional case, frontier row 'Last fall degree of zero-dimensional Weil descent systems') to positive-dimensional systems, which is the shape of the programme's relation-collection systems before specialising the target. Possibly gives a proof route for lever 1 ('degree-c pseudo-solutions' vs. a transfer theorem from the original S_{m+1} over F_{2^n} to its descent).
papers.suggested_route: Read the theorem statement; if it bounds d_F(descended S_{m+1} restricted to an l-dim subspace) in terms of d_F of the un-descended system plus a function of l and m independent of n, that is exactly the 'bound f(m) independent of n' the brief says would revive the heuristics. Toy check: compute d_F of un-descended S_3, S_4 over F_{2^n} for n=13..31 with msolve (should be small and n-independent) and compare with the programme's measured descended D = ceil(l/2)+4 at m=3 to see whether the transfer inequality is tight.

papers.title: On index calculus algorithms for subfield curves
papers.authors: Steven D. Galbraith, Robert Granger, Simon-Philipp Merz, Christophe Petit
papers.summary: Factor bases invariant under the q-power Frobenius of F_{q^n} for subfield (Koblitz-type) curves; n^2 speedup of the linear algebra; Frobenius used for symmetry breaking in the polynomial systems; experimental study of solving costs; notes the Gorla-Massierer trace-zero approach gave no dramatic speedup.
papers.relevance: Frontier known_mechanism 'Frobenius-invariant factor bases for subfield (Koblitz) curves'; atlas LEAD-ICB-frobenius-orbit-factor-base closed_obstructed. Polynomial gains only.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Cover attacks for elliptic curves with prime order
papers.authors: Song Tian
papers.summary: For some prime-order E/F_{q^3}, an F_q-rational (l,l,l)-isogeny from the Weil restriction (a 3-dimensional abelian variety) to the Jacobian of a genus-3 curve over F_q, then Diem's Õ(q) index calculus; no covering map used.
papers.relevance: Ingredient: Weil restriction of dimension n >= 3 isogenous to a Jacobian. Over F_p the Weil restriction is E itself (dimension 1): nothing to glue. Atlas: LEAD-TRF-weil-restriction-jacobian-class open_next_step ('genus-n Jacobians in the isogeny class of a Weil-restricted elliptic curve') and LEAD-TRF-small-genus-cover-general closed_obstructed.
papers.suggested_route: Only for composite-degree or F_{p^k} targets already filed; none for F_p or F_{2^131}.

papers.title: Extending the GLS endomorphism to speed up GHS Weil descent using Magma
papers.authors: Jesús-Javier Chi-Domínguez, Francisco Rodríguez-Henríquez, Benjamin Smith
papers.summary: A GLS endomorphism on the binary elliptic curve descends to the GHS hyperelliptic Jacobian and gives a factor-n speedup of the index calculus there; large computed example.
papers.relevance: Symmetry gains inside a known (GHS, composite degree) attack; polynomial. Atlas LEAD-TRF-ghs-binary-composite closed_known.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH (and the Maino-Martindale-Panny-Pope-Wesolowski direct attack; Robert's 8-dimensional variant)
papers.authors: Wouter Castryck, Thomas Decru; Luciano Maino, Chloe Martindale, Lorenz Panny, Giacomo Pope, Benjamin Wesolowski; Damien Robert
papers.summary: Kani's reducibility criterion: from the images of a torsion basis E[N] under a secret isogeny of known degree d with N^2 > d, build an (N,N)-isogeny of E^2 (or E^4/E^8 without End of the starting curve, Robert) one of whose components is the secret; heuristically polynomial time; SIKEp434 broken in ~10 min.
papers.relevance: Ingredient = torsion-point information about a map of KNOWN degree. For ECDLP the 'map' is [k] of unknown degree k^2 and we know its value on a single point; torsion images on E[N] for N coprime to r are useless (they are k mod N, and E[N] is not rational anyway), and for N=r they ARE the DLP. Atlas LEAD-TRF-second-torsion-direction (Kani/Robert graph kernels, Richelot gluing) closed_obstructed.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Some applications of higher dimensional isogenies to elliptic curves (overview of results)
papers.authors: Damien Robert
papers.summary: Embedding lemma applications: (1) End(E) of an ORDINARY curve over F_q in time polynomial in log q given the factorisation of Delta_pi (hence quantum polynomial); (2) canonical lift of an ordinary curve to precision m in quasi-linear time, giving point counting in Õ(n^2 log^{O(1)} p); (3) quasi-linear unconditional CRT algorithm for Siegel modular polynomials; generalisation to ordinary abelian varieties; revision notes that lifts do not seem to help attack commutative isogeny-based cryptography.
papers.relevance: Two atlas items are affected as TOOLS: LEAD-TRF-cm-canonical-lift-heights (closed_obstructed by heights, independent of how fast the lift is computed) and LEAD-STR-class-group-ecdlp-bridge open_next_step (End(E) now cheap). Neither closure's hypothesis changes.
papers.suggested_route: Cheap re-check of the heights closure with the fast canonical lift as oracle: lift E/F_p (p ~ 2^20-2^30, CM small disc) and its factor base to the canonical lift over Z_p to precision m, measure p-adic 'size' statistics of lifted sums vs lifted summands; the closure predicts no sub-additive size appears (the canonical lift is a formal-group statement, not a height-compressing global one).

papers.title: Introducing Clapoti(s): evaluating the isogeny class group action in polynomial time; PEGASIS: practical effective class group action using 4-dimensional isogenies (and qt-Pegasis, dimension 2)
papers.authors: Aurel Page, Damien Robert (2023); Pierrick Dartois, Jonathan Komada Eriksen, et al. (2025); qt-Pegasis authors not verified
papers.date: ePrint 2023/1766 (2023-11); ePrint 2025/401 (2025-03), CRYPTO 2025; qt-Pegasis 2025/26 (IACR news item, not opened)
papers.summary: Clapoti: randomized polynomial-time evaluation of E -> E/E[a] for any ideal class a of the orientation order, O((log Delta + log q)^{O(1)}); PEGASIS makes it practical with 4-dimensional isogenies (no class-group structure, no expensive lattice reduction); qt-Pegasis uses dimension 2 and is 1.8-2.6x faster at 500-4000-bit parameters.
papers.relevance: The class-group action on ordinary/oriented curves is now a cheap primitive. For ECDLP: Transport conservation says every homomorphic transfer changes decomposition counts by exactly |kernel|^{m-1}; the action only reaches other curves in the same isogeny class with the same group order (Tate). Relevant to LEAD-STR-class-group-ecdlp-bridge and LEAD-STR-class-representative-ic-selection (both open_next_step) as an enabler, not as a mechanism.
papers.suggested_route: Enabler for LEAD-STR-class-representative-ic-selection: with a cheap action one can scan the whole crater of a small-discriminant toy curve for the model minimising the measured solving degree; the closure LEAD-ICE-curve-presentation-invariance (open_next_step) predicts no change in D.

papers.title: Weak instances of class group action based cryptography via self-pairings
papers.authors: Wouter Castryck, Marc Houben, Simon-Philipp Merz, Marzio Mula, Sam van Buuren, Frederik Vercauteren
papers.summary: Self-pairings with cyclic domain compatible with isogenies between curves oriented by an imaginary quadratic order; yields polynomial-time attacks on class-group-action instances when the degree of the secret isogeny is known, with concrete ordinary-curve examples; streamlines the DDH-for-class-group-actions results of Castryck-Houben-Vercauteren-Wesolowski 2022.
papers.relevance: Ingredient: a self-pairing (bilinear E x E -> mu) that is non-degenerate on a cyclic subgroup; exists only with the orientation and a known degree. The programme's LEAD-ICP-self-pairing-prime-order and LEAD-TRF-one-point-self-pairing are closed_obstructed (no non-degenerate self-pairing on a prime-order subgroup of a curve with trivial pairing), and this paper's conditions confirm the scope.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: The supersingular isogeny path and endomorphism ring problems are equivalent; Unconditional foundations for supersingular isogeny-based cryptography; The supersingular Endomorphism Ring and One Endomorphism problems are equivalent
papers.authors: Benjamin Wesolowski (2021); Arthur Herlédan Le Merdy, Benjamin Wesolowski (2025); Aurel Page, Benjamin Wesolowski (2023)
papers.summary: Path-finding in supersingular l-isogeny graphs, EndRing, MaxOrder and OneEnd are polynomially equivalent (GRH, later unconditional), with worst-case to average-case reductions; CSIDH security equivalent to the (oriented) endomorphism ring problem (Wesolowski Eurocrypt 2022).
papers.relevance: Shows the isogeny world's hardness is governed by one complete invariant (End) with checkable algebraic structure. ECDLP has no such invariant inside E(F_q): End(E) is known or cheaply computable for every deployed curve (CM order) and tells nothing about k. Atlas: LEAD-STR-isogeny-class-generic-invariance, LEAD-STR-torsion-module-leak closed_obstructed.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: The supersingular isogeny problem in time and memory p^{1/3+o(1)}, unconditionally; Smoothness of shortest isogenies to Frobenius conjugates
papers.authors: José Luis Delgado (2026-09); Yi Ouyang, Wei Wei, Zheng Xu (2026-10)
papers.summary: Delgado: Las Vegas p^{1/3} algorithm for OneEnd without the smoothness heuristic, by fixing a family of smooth degrees, using counting results for isogenies to Frobenius conjugates, a collision estimate for the random walk, and a meet-in-the-middle split of the degree; compose with Frobenius to get a non-scalar endomorphism. Ouyang-Wei-Xu: bounds on the smoothness probability of the minimal degree delta_E of isogenies E -> E^{(p)}, making Wesolowski's p^{1/3} attack unconditional; asymptotic formula for the existence probability of a degree-n connecting isogeny in terms of Dirichlet L-values.
papers.relevance: Newest structural results in the lane (within 2026-09-15..10-31). The 'smoothness' lives on isogeny DEGREES (integers represented by a quadratic form), a genuine sub-multiplicative size - but it measures distance in the isogeny graph, not the position of a point in E(F_q). No ECDLP analogue; supersingular only.
papers.suggested_route: None for ECDLP. Possibly useful to the programme's rigour culture: the 'fix a smooth family in advance + counting + collision estimate' pattern is how one would make a Semaev-style yield heuristic rigorous if yields ever mattered (they do not: monodromy closure).

papers.title: Climbing and descending tall isogeny volcanos
papers.authors: Steven D. Galbraith
papers.date: ePrint 2024/924 (2024-06-10, rev. 2025-07-24); Research in Number Theory 11 (2025)
papers.summary: Revisits relating ECDLP instances across ordinary curves with the same number of points (Galbraith 1999; Jao-Miller-Venkatesan 2005): rigorous Õ(q^{1/4}) isogeny computation within the class for flat volcanoes (random curves) and tall volcanoes with small craters (pairing-friendly), heuristic worst case improved from q^{1.5} to q^{0.4} using Kani-type constructions; explicitly motivated by pre-quantum ordinary-curve ECC.
papers.relevance: Strengthens the random self-reduction (LEAD-STR-jmv-random-self-reduction closed_known) but by Transport conservation and Tate's theorem it cannot create a weak neighbour (LEAD-STR-isogeny-walk-weak-neighbour closed_known). A 2024-25 result the atlas may not cite; it changes constants of an already-closed lead.
papers.suggested_route: None (closure scope unchanged); update the JMV lead card's cost from q^{1.5} to q^{1/4}/q^{0.4}.

papers.title: The Structured Generic-Group Model
papers.authors: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs, Alexandra Henzinger, David J. Wu
papers.summary: Extends Shoup's GGM to algorithms that exploit non-generic structure of at most a delta fraction of the group elements (precise definition of 'exploit'); any such DL algorithm in a prime-order-q group needs Omega(min(sqrt q, 1/delta)) time; tight subexponential lower bound for algorithms exploiting the multiplicative structure of smooth integers but otherwise generic (covers a broad class of index calculus); similar bounds for small integers, smooth polynomials and ELLIPTIC-CURVE POINTS.
papers.relevance: Formalises the brief's rule 5 from a different direction: the programme's certificate is B.D^2 << N (CGK preprocessing); the structured GGM says that if the only non-generic step is 'recognise membership in a delta-dense structured set' then time >= min(sqrt r, 1/delta) = min(sqrt r, r/B). Every factor-base index calculus with B < sqrt r base points is therefore bounded below by r/B unless the DECOMPOSITION step itself is non-generic in the structured sense - which is the programme's 'the only door is the field representation'. Gives the exact definition of 'exploit' the programme can quote.
papers.suggested_route: Theory + toy: (1) write each programme pipeline (compact-orbit k-sum, pair table, Semaev decomposition) as a structured-GGM algorithm, identify delta and which step is non-generic under the paper's definition, and derive the implied lower bound; compare with the measured 2^25-2^27 gap to the CGK line. (2) Check whether their 'elliptic-curve points' structured model matches 'x in a subspace/window' bases; if their bound is tight for that model, the lever-8 x-functional filter must exploit structure OUTSIDE their definition, which sharpens KN-OPEN-91d4f6 into a precise target. No security claim; this is a lower-bound bookkeeping exercise.

papers.title: A new approach to generic lower bounds: classical/quantum MDL, quantum factoring, and more
papers.authors: Minki Hhan
papers.summary: Compression-lemma proofs of GGM lower bounds for multiple-instance and one-more DL (classical and quantum, allowing classical preprocessing), order finding and factoring in a generic ring model, and a lower bound for 'basic index calculus' in a new idealized group model involving smooth numbers.
papers.relevance: Second recent formal treatment of index calculus as a restricted non-generic model; together with 2026/384 it supplies the proof technique (compression) that the programme's own certificates (B.D^2 vs N) could be rephrased in. Multi-instance bounds also cover the programme's multi-target closures.
papers.suggested_route: Cite alongside 2026/384; no experiment.

papers.title: Bounds on polynomial approximations of the discrete logarithm function
papers.authors: Swastik Kopparty, Rishabh Kothary, Ashutosh Shankar
papers.summary: Improves Coppersmith-Shparlinski: a univariate polynomial of degree <= D over F_p agrees with log_g on at most ~sqrt(Dp) inputs (matching the Johnson bound, via list decoding; non-trivial even for D > p/2); for D=1 an O(p^{2/5}) bound via sum-product; improved bounds for bivariate polynomials vanishing on (x, dlog x). Elliptic curves not mentioned.
papers.relevance: A rigorous wall on the F_p^* version of the programme's lever 8 / lever 12 (x-functional filters, learned predictors, coordinate-statistic hunts): no low-degree polynomial of the element correlates with its log beyond sqrt(Dp) points. The EC analogue (polynomial interpolation of the ECDLP in x(P); classical Lange-Winterhof results, not re-verified here) would bound any polynomial x-filter's correlation with the discrete log, though the open lever 8 asks for correlation with SUMS, not with logs.
papers.suggested_route: Toy falsifier for lever 8 restricted to polynomial filters: on E/F_p (p ~ 2^16-2^20), for degree D <= 8 enumerate/least-squares the best polynomial f(x) in F_p[x] (or Boolean filters of x bits of bounded degree) such that f(x(P+Q)) is predicted from f(x(P)), f(x(Q)) better than chance; the KKS/list-decoding argument predicts agreement O(sqrt(Dp)); if the measured single-bucket gain stays within that bound at all D, lever 8 is closed for polynomial filters and only non-polynomial (lattice/bit-level) filters remain.

papers.title: The Cokernel Pairing
papers.authors: Krijn Reijnders
papers.summary: Defines a pairing on the rational cokernels E(F_q)/[m]E(F_q) (complementing Weil on ker[m] and Tate on ker x coker); non-degenerate when E[m] c E(F_q), computable from three Tate pairings and two DLs in mu_m given an E[m] basis; applications to Sylow l-torsion bases and l^k-isogeny computation.
papers.relevance: A new (2026) pairing object, but its non-degeneracy needs full rational m-torsion; for the prime-order subgroup of a deployed curve (m = r) this forces r | q-1, i.e. embedding degree 1 - the MOV wall (LEAD-TRF-mov-small-embedding-degree closed_known; LEAD-ICP-self-pairing-prime-order closed_obstructed). Not a door.
papers.suggested_route: One-line check: on a prime-order toy curve with embedding degree > 1 verify the cokernel pairing on E(F_q)/[r]E(F_q) is trivial/undefined (E[r] not rational), confirming the closure scope; no further work.

papers.title: Graphs and cycles in curve-based collision walks
papers.authors: Sebastiano Boscardin, Jolijn Cottaar, Monika Trimoska
papers.summary: Multi-user van Oorschot-Wiener collision attacks on ECDLP and on supersingular isogeny path-finding over F_{p^2} and F_p; new pseudorandom walks for isogeny path-finding; L keys from L collisions for ECDLP (baseline), ~L from L + log L collisions for the F_{p^2} isogeny problem, 0.75L (with infiltrator) over F_p.
papers.relevance: Rho/multi-target bookkeeping; ECDLP is only the comparison baseline. Covered by LEAD-RHO-dp-multitarget-precomputation closed_known and the BL equal-advice audits.
papers.suggested_route: None for IC; the ECDLP multi-user figure (L keys from L collisions) can be quoted as the generic baseline in the report.

papers.title: A Las Vegas algorithm to solve the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem; A guess and determine attack on the ECDLP
papers.authors: Ayan Mahalanobis, Vivek Mallick (2018); Ayan Mahalanobis (2026)
papers.summary: Non-generic Las Vegas ECDLP method reducing to finding a zero minor in a matrix over the base field (functions in a Riemann-Roch space vanishing on a chosen subset of points); the 2026 paper uses the intersection poset of a hyperplane arrangement to find zero minors; no complexity bound stated in either abstract and no claim to beat sqrt.
papers.relevance: A 'relation search by linear algebra on evaluations' idea: pick 3n points, look for a function in L(nO) vanishing on n+... of them; the search for a zero minor is itself exponential. Not in the atlas by name; it is a generic-oracle-with-advice in disguise unless the minor search uses field structure.
papers.suggested_route: Low priority: price the zero-minor search at toy scale (p ~ 2^20, n = 3..6) in GAE and place it against the B.D^2 certificate; expected to land far above rho like the k-sum pipelines.
